Exodus

Wheel of Heaven Translation

The seven Raëlian-canon-cited chapters: the burning bush, the Passover/firstborn institution, the parting of the sea, the manna, the rock-water + Amalek, the Sinai theophany, the Decalogue

Direct Direct Established or uncontested across mainstream sources, or a direct description of the project itself. Framework Framework Foundational premise of the Wheel of Heaven framework. Explicit in the Raëlian canon; not endorsed by mainstream scholarship. Inferred Inferred A reasonable reading of comparative material — not stated literally, but consistent with the source. Speculative Speculative Interpretive synthesis or hypothesis that goes beyond what any single source states.

An English translation of the seven Exodus chapters the Raëlian canon engages in *The Truth* (Genesis-Exodus exegetical sequence) and *The Book Which Tells the Truth*: **Exodus 3** (the burning bush + the *ehyeh asher ehyeh* divine-name revelation); **Exodus 13** (the consecration of the firstborn + the pillar of cloud and fire); **Exodus 14** (the parting of the sea); **Exodus 16** (the manna and the quail); **Exodus 17** (the water from the rock at Massah-Meribah + the battle with Amalek); **Exodus 19** (the Sinai theophany — the descent of YHWH on the mountain in fire, smoke, and trumpet-blast); **Exodus 20** (the Decalogue + the altar law). Source: Sefaria v3 API Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain). Same source-acquisition pattern as the Genesis precedent in this project. This is the second-most-canonically-engaged Hebrew Bible book in the Raëlian corpus after Genesis. The chapter selection reflects the canon's specific chapter-and-verse citations: Ex 3 (the burning bush and the divine-name revelation in *The Truth*); Ex 13-14 (the Passover-and-parting-of-the-sea narrative — the canon's reading of the parting as 'a physical demonstration' of Elohim technology; *Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet*); Ex 16-17 (the manna and water-from-rock — read as 'engineered nutrition technology' in the canon's framework); Ex 19-20 (the Sinai theophany — the canon's most-explicit 'Elohim-craft descent on the mountain' citation, with the Decalogue read as 'the engineered laws given to humanity'). The WoH-Translation produces the philologically-disciplined version of these passages, with explicit operational disavowals against the Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-craft reading of Ex 14 + Ex 19, Christian-typology pre-resolution (no Red-Sea-as-baptism, no manna-as-eucharist, no Sinai-as-old-covenant-superseded), and the Raëlian-canon's pre-filtered readings — acknowledgment-without-endorsement, per the Shi'ur Qomah *parasangs* and Qur'an *inshiqāq al-qamar* precedents.

Chapter 3

Exodus 3 — The burning bush + the divine-name revelation (ehyeh asher ehyeh)

1
Now Moses was shepherding the flock of Yitro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian. He led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to the mountain of the Elohim, to Horeb.
Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):
וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל־הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה׃
Notes Verse 1

The opening locates Moses at har hā-ʾĕlōhîm ḥōrēḇāh 'the mountain of the Elohim, to Horeb' — the divine-mountain that the Exodus tradition variously names Horeb (E-tradition / Deuteronomic) and Sinai (J/P-tradition). See the central entry har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus for the source-critical Horeb/Sinai variation and the cross-corpus reach to the broader Northwest-Semitic cosmic-mountain tradition (Clifford 1972 The Cosmic Mountain in Canaan and the Old Testament; Day 2000 Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan).

2
And the messenger of YHWH appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush. He looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not consumed.
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
וַ֠יֵּרָא מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו בְּלַבַּת־אֵ֖שׁ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַסְּנֶה֙ בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְהַסְּנֶ֖ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֻכָּֽל׃
Notes Verse 2

The malʾaḵ YHWH 'messenger of YHWH' appears at v 2; v 4 identifies the speaker as YHWH and the Elohim. This is the classic malakh-YHWH-as-YHWH fluidity-of-divine-bodies pattern documented by Sommer 2009 The Bodies of God and the World of Ancient Israel and at the central entry. Cross-corpus parallels at Gen 16, 22, Judg 6, 13. The sneh 'thorn-bush' lexeme is hapax-rare and carries possible wordplay to sinay.

3
And Moses said, "Let me turn aside now and see this great sight — why the bush is not burned up."
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה־נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא־יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה׃
4
When YHWH saw that he had turned aside to see, the Elohim called to him from the midst of the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he said, "Here I am."
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
וַיַּ֥רְא יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י סָ֣ר לִרְא֑וֹת וַיִּקְרָא֩ אֵלָ֨יו אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֗ה וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃
Notes Verse 4

The doubled-name calling mōšeh mōšeh (cf. Gen 22:11 avraham avraham; Gen 46:2 yaʿaqov yaʿaqov; 1 Sam 3:10 šĕmuʾēl šĕmuʾēl) is the theophanic-doubled-name calling-formula. Moses' response hinnēnî 'here I am' is the prophetic-response formula deployed elsewhere by Abraham (Gen 22:1, 11), Jacob (Gen 31:11, 46:2), Samuel (1 Sam 3:4, 6, 8), and Isaiah (Isa 6:8).

5
And he said, "Do not draw near here. Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground."
And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: and Joseph was in Egypt already.
וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תִּקְרַ֣ב הֲלֹ֑ם שַׁל־נְעָלֶ֙יךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עוֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו אַדְמַת־קֹ֖דֶשׁ הֽוּא׃
6
And he said, "I am the Elohim of your father, the Elohim of Avraham, the Elohim of Yitzchaq, and the Elohim of Ya'aqov." And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at the Elohim.
And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיַּסְתֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנָ֔יו כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א מֵהַבִּ֖יט אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
Notes Verse 6

The patriarchal-God-of-the-fathers formula with the threefold ʾĕlōhê repetition (preserved on the surface, not smoothed to a single 'Elohim of Avraham-Yitzchaq-and-Yaaqov') establishes the covenantal-continuity between the Sinai revelation and the patriarchal narratives of Genesis. See the central entry elohei-avraham-yitzchaq-veyaakov-patriarchal-god-formula-cross-corpus for the Albright-Alt-de Vaux tradition-historical framework and the NT cross-corpus at Mark 12:26-27 with operational disavowals.

7
And YHWH said, "I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Mitsrayim, and I have heard their cry on account of their taskmasters; indeed, I know their pains.
And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה רָאֹ֥ה רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־עֳנִ֥י עַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־צַעֲקָתָ֤ם שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י נֹֽגְשָׂ֔יו כִּ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־מַכְאֹבָֽיו׃
Notes Verse 7

The doubled infinitive-absolute rāʾōh rāʾîṯî 'I have surely seen' (cf. Gen 16:11, 31:42) is the emphatic-divine-attention formula; the WoH-Translation preserves the doubled-verb force ('I have surely seen') per the ASV-baseline convention rather than the JPS smoothing ('I have marked well').

8
And I have come down to deliver them from the hand of Mitsrayim and to bring them up out of that land to a good and broad land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.
Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
וָאֵרֵ֞ד לְהַצִּיל֣וֹ ׀ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֗יִם וּֽלְהַעֲלֹתוֹ֮ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִוא֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ טוֹבָה֙ וּרְחָבָ֔ה אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ אֶל־מְק֤וֹם הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
9
And now, behold, the cry of the children of Yisra'el has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־הַלַּ֔חַץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹחֲצִ֥ים אֹתָֽם׃
10
And now, go, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Yisra'el, out of Mitsrayim."
come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they also join themselves unto our enemies, and fight against us, and get them up out of the land.
וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְאֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֖ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְהוֹצֵ֛א אֶת־עַמִּ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
11
And Moses said to the Elohim, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Yisra'el out of Mitsrayim?"
Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים מִ֣י אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אֵלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְכִ֥י אוֹצִ֛יא אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
Notes Verse 11

Moses' first commission-refusal mî ʾānōḵî 'who am I' is the prophetic-commission-refusal formula deployed across the prophetic-call narratives (Jer 1:6 'I am only a youth'; Judg 6:15 Gideon's 'my clan is the weakest'; 1 Sam 9:21 Saul's 'I am only a Benjamite'). The pattern is the prophet's-initial-protest-followed-by-divine-reassurance form-critical structure.

12
And he said, "For I will be with you, and this shall be the sign for you that I have sent you: when you bring the people out of Mitsrayim, you shall serve the Elohim on this mountain."
But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כִּֽי־אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י שְׁלַחְתִּ֑יךָ בְּהוֹצִֽיאֲךָ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם תַּֽעַבְדוּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
Notes Verse 12

kî-ʾehyeh ʿimmāḵ 'for I will be with you' deploys the same ʾehyeh verbal form that recurs at v 14 in the divine-name-revelation; the verses are deliberately paired by the Hebrew narrative. Propp 1999 ad loc. argues that this v-12 / v-14 ʾehyeh connection supports the future-aspectual 'I will be' reading of the divine-name (rather than the KJV traditional 'I am'). See the central entry ehyeh-asher-ehyeh-divine-name-revelation-ex-3-14-cross-corpus for the multi-stratum reading-history.

13
And Moses said to the Elohim, "Behold, I am going to the children of Yisra'el and I will say to them, 'The Elohim of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they will say to me, 'What is his name?' What shall I say to them?"
And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigor:
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֣י בָא֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לָהֶ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְאָֽמְרוּ־לִ֣י מַה־שְּׁמ֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵהֶֽם׃
14
And the Elohim said to Moses, "I am that I am." And he said, "Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el: 'I am has sent me to you.'"
and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field, all their service, wherein they made them serve with rigor.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽהְיֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
Notes Verse 14

THE divine-name-revelation site of the Hebrew Bible. The three-word formula ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh is the single most-discussed lexical-philological site of the Tanakh. The WoH-Translation preserves the KJV/RSV traditional 'I am that I am' as the surface English-rendering; the five major reading-strata (KJV present-stative; JPS/Propp future-aspectual; LXX ho ōn; Albright causative-hiphʿil; process-theology becoming-one) are documented at the central entry ehyeh-asher-ehyeh-divine-name-revelation-ex-3-14-cross-corpus. Operational disavowals: no Christological pre-resolution (no 'ehyeh = preincarnate Christ via John 8:58'); no Raëlian-canon 'engineered-AI-presence-designator' reading; no Sitchin 'Anunnaki-faction-self-identification' fringe-reading. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement of the Raëlian-canon's engagement in The Truth, per the Shi'ur Qomah parasangs precedent and the Qur'an inshiqāq al-qamar precedent.

15
And the Elohim said further to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el: 'YHWH, the Elohim of your fathers, the Elohim of Avraham, the Elohim of Yitzchaq, and the Elohim of Ya'aqov, has sent me to you. This is my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation.'
And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ע֨וֹד אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כֹּֽה־תֹאמַר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם זֶה־שְּׁמִ֣י לְעֹלָ֔ם וְזֶ֥ה זִכְרִ֖י לְדֹ֥ר דֹּֽר׃
Notes Verse 15

The full-name revelation YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăḇōṯêḵem 'YHWH the Elohim of your fathers' with the threefold patriarchal-name expansion; zeh-šĕmî lĕ-ʿōlām 'this is my name forever'. The verse pairs the explicit YHWH-tetragrammaton with the v-14 ʾehyeh construct; cross-corpus to Ex 6:2-3 (the P-source name-revelation tradition) — the documentary-hypothesis tension is preserved without adjudication.

16
Go and gather the elders of Yisra'el and say to them, 'YHWH, the Elohim of your fathers, has appeared to me — the Elohim of Avraham, Yitzchaq, and Ya'aqov — saying: I have surely visited you and what is being done to you in Mitsrayim,
and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the birth-stool; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him; but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
לֵ֣ךְ וְאָֽסַפְתָּ֞ אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵהֶם֙ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִרְאָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם יִצְחָ֥ק וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר פָּקֹ֤ד פָּקַ֙דְתִּי֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הֶעָשׂ֥וּי לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
Notes Verse 16

The doubled pāqōd pāqaḏtî 'I have surely visited' is the Exodus-formula deliberately picking up Gen 50:24-25 (the Joseph promise: pāqōḏ yip̄qōḏ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯḵem 'the Elohim will surely visit you'). See the existing entry paqod-yiphqod-divine-visitation-exodus-formula-cross-corpus.

17
and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Mitsrayim to the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.'
But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men-children alive.
וָאֹמַ֗ר אַעֲלֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶם֮ מֵעֳנִ֣י מִצְרַיִם֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

Notes Verse 18

ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿiḇriyyîm 'the Elohim of the Hebrews' — first deployment of the Hebrews-as-ethnonym in the WoH-Exodus translation. See the existing entry ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology for the Hebrew-designation tradition and the cross-corpus reach.

Notes Verse 22

nāṣaltem ʾeṯ-miṣrayim 'you shall despoil Mitsrayim' — the Israelite-women-asking-for-silver/gold/clothing institution. The verb nṣl (Piʿel) 'to strip, despoil' is preserved on the surface rather than smoothed to 'plunder' or 'ask of'. Cross-corpus to Ex 12:35-36 (the Passover-narrative recall of the same institution). The moral-theological dispute over the despoiling-of-Egypt is documented in the rabbinic, patristic, and modern-critical reception (Childs 1974 ad loc.); the WoH-Translation preserves the literal Hebrew without softening.

Exodus 13 — The consecration of the firstborn + the pillar of cloud and fire

The divine-routing-detour decision — Israel led not via the Philistine coastal route (the 'Way of Horus' / via maris, the shortest route) but via the wilderness-of-the-Reed-Sea route. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and YHWH drove back the sea by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were split apart.

Notes Verse 21

The strong-east-wind operative-mechanism: bĕ-rûaḥ qāḏîm ʿazzâ kol-ha-laylâ 'by a strong east wind all night'. The east-wind agency is preserved on the surface; the naturalistic-academic east-wind-tidal-event reading (Hoffmeier 2005) concentrates here. The waters-split-apart wa-yibbāqʿû ha-mmāyim deploys the bqʿ chaoskampf-vocabulary.

Notes Verse 22

The wall-of-water imagery: wĕ-ha-mayim lāhem ḥōmâ mî-mînām ū-mi-śmōʾlām 'the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left'. The literal ḥōmâ 'wall' is preserved on the surface; the cross-corpus echo at Josh 3:13-17 (the Jordan-stoppage at the entry into the Land) deploys the same wall-of-water imagery.

YHWH looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud in the ʾašmōreṯ ha-bōqer 'morning watch' (the third night-watch). The pillar's surveillance-function deploys the divine-presence-marker in a divine-warrior register.

ha-yyāḏ ha-gĕḏōlâ 'the great hand' — the divine-warrior-victory-formula closing the chapter. Exodus 16 — The manna and the quail

1
And they journeyed from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Yisra'el came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their going out from the land of Mitsrayim.

The mān-hûʾ etymological-question 'what is it?' establishes the folk-etymological aetiology of the substance-name. Chapter 17

Exodus 17 — The water from the rock at Massah-Meribah + the battle with Amalek

1
And the whole congregation of the children of Yisra'el journeyed from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, according to the mouth of YHWH; and they camped at Refidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
And afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
וַ֠יִּסְעוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃
Notes Verse 1

Arrival at Refidim; the wilderness-water-crisis sets up the Massah-Meribah aetiological-naming at v 7.

2
And the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test YHWH?"
And Pharaoh said, Who is Jehovah, that I should hearken unto his voice to let Israel go? I know not Jehovah, and moreover I will not let Israel go.
וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן֙ עִמָּדִ֔י מַה־תְּנַסּ֖וּן אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
Notes Verse 2

The rîḇ 'quarrel, contention' verb deployed twice; the lexeme will become the Mĕrîḇâ place-name at v 7. The nsh (Piʿel) 'to test' verb sets up the Massâ place-name.

3
And the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured against Moses, and said, "Why is this — that you have brought us up out of Mitsrayim to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"
And they said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days` journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice unto Jehovah our God, lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.
וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י וְאֶת־בָּנַ֥י וְאֶת־מִקְנַ֖י בַּצָּמָֽא׃
4
And Moses cried out to YHWH, saying, "What shall I do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."
And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, loose the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.
וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה ע֥וֹד מְעַ֖ט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי׃
5
And YHWH said to Moses, "Pass on before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Yisra'el; and your staff, with which you struck the Nile — take in your hand and go.
And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land are now many, and ye make them rest from their burdens.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃
6
Behold, I am standing before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out from it, and the people shall drink." And Moses did so before the eyes of the elders of Yisra'el.
And the same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
הִנְנִ֣י עֹמֵד֩ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ שָּׁ֥ם ׀ עַֽל־הַצּוּר֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַצּ֗וּר וְיָצְא֥וּ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ מַ֖יִם וְשָׁתָ֣ה הָעָ֑ם וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Notes Verse 6

ha-ṣṣûr bĕ-ḥōrēḇ 'the rock at Horeb' — explicit localization at the divine-mountain. The ṣûr 'rock' lexeme has cross-corpus reach as a divine-epithet (Deut 32:4, 32:18 YHWH as ṣûr; Isa 26:4; Ps 18:2, 31:3, 62:7); the Rock-as-divine-epithet tradition is a documented Hebrew Bible feature. Operational disavowals at the central entry maśśah-merivah-testing-contention-place-name-aetiological-cross-corpus: no Christological pre-resolution of the rock (against 1 Cor 10:4 'the rock was Christ'); no engineered-installation Sitchin/Raëlian-canon reading.

7
And he called the name of the place Massah (Testing) and Meribah (Quarreling), because of the quarreling of the children of Yisra'el and because of their testing of YHWH, saying, "Is YHWH in our midst, or not?"
Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.
וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֔וֹם מַסָּ֖ה וּמְרִיבָ֑ה עַל־רִ֣יב ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְעַ֨ל נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲיֵ֧שׁ יְהוָ֛ה בְּקִרְבֵּ֖נוּ אִם־אָֽיִן׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 7

The Massah-Meribah aetiological-naming: wa-yyiqrāʾ šēm ha-māqôm massâ ū-mĕrîḇâ 'and he called the name of the place Massah (Testing) and Meribah (Quarreling)'. The doubled-naming establishes the foundational covenantal-recall paradigm of Israelite-disbelief. Cross-corpus to Deut 6:16, 9:22, 33:8, Ps 95:8-9, Heb 3:7-19, 4:1-11.

8
And Amaleq came and fought with Yisra'el at Refidim.
And the number of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish aught thereof: for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
וַיָּבֹ֖א עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּרְפִידִֽם׃
Notes Verse 8

The Amalek-attack initiation-verse. Amaleq's attack at Refidim establishes the Amalek-as-perennial-enemy theological-pattern. See the central entry amalek-perennial-enemy-ex-17-deut-25-1-sam-15-esther-cross-corpus for the cross-corpus chain (Deut 25:17-19 → 1 Sam 15 → Esther) and the operational disavowals against modern political weaponization, Christian-supersessionist inversion, and Sitchin/Raëlian fringe-readings.

9
And Moses said to Yehoshua, "Choose men for us and go out, fight with Amaleq. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of the Elohim in my hand."
Let heavier work be laid upon the men, that they may labor therein; and let them not regard lying words.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ בְּחַר־לָ֣נוּ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְצֵ֖א הִלָּחֵ֣ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק מָחָ֗ר אָנֹכִ֤י נִצָּב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וּמַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדִֽי׃
Notes Verse 9

Yehošuaʿ — first appearance of the future leader. The WoH-Translation preserves the Hebrew transliteration 'Yehoshua' per the project's Genesis-precedent register rather than smoothing to the English-tradition 'Joshua'. maṭṭê hā-ʾĕlōhîm 'the staff of the Elohim' — the divine-instrument designation.

10
And Yehoshua did as Moses had said to him, to fight with Amaleq; and Moses, Aharon, and Chur went up to the top of the hill.
And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.
וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽמַר־לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְח֔וּר עָל֖וּ רֹ֥אשׁ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
11
And it came to pass, when Moses raised his hand, that Yisra'el prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amaleq prevailed.
Go yourselves, get you straw where ye can find it: for nought of your work shall be diminished.
וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥ים מֹשֶׁ֛ה יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנִ֛יחַ יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֥ר עֲמָלֵֽק׃
Notes Verse 11

The raised-hands-of-Moses ritual-instrument pattern. The midrashic-rabbinic tradition (Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael, Amalek 1; m. Rosh Hashanah 3:8) reads the raised-hands not as magical-instrument but as Israel-orientation-to-divine-presence.

12
And the hands of Moses were heavy; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aharon and Chur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
וִידֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ כְּבֵדִ֔ים וַיִּקְחוּ־אֶ֛בֶן וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב עָלֶ֑יהָ וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י יָדָ֛יו אֱמוּנָ֖ה עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
13
And Yehoshua disabled Amaleq and his people with the edge of the sword.
And the taskmasters were urgent saying, Fulfil your works, [your] daily tasks, as when there was straw.
וַיַּחֲלֹ֧שׁ יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־עֲמָלֵ֥ק וְאֶת־עַמּ֖וֹ לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃ (פ)
14
And YHWH said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in the book, and place it in the ears of Yehoshua: for I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amaleq from under the heavens."
And the officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh`s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task both yesterday and to-day, in making brick as heretofore?
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּתֹ֨ב זֹ֤את זִכָּרוֹן֙ בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וְשִׂ֖ים בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּֽי־מָחֹ֤ה אֶמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
Notes Verse 14

The divine-curse-of-Amalek: māḥōh ʾemḥeh ʾeṯ zēḵer ʿămālēq mit-taḥaṯ ha-šāmāyim 'I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amaleq from under the heavens'. The doubled-verb māḥōh ʾemḥeh deploys the same emcheh-erasure root as Gen 6:7 (the Flood-erasure); the existing entry emcheh documents the cross-corpus root-deployment. The genocidal-language of the Hebrew Bible's Amalek-curse is preserved on the surface; the WoH-Translation explicitly disavows any modern political identification with the Amalek-figure (see the central entry).

15
And Moses built an altar and called its name YHWH-Nissi (YHWH is my banner).
Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?
וַיִּ֥בֶן מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ נִסִּֽי׃
Notes Verse 15

YHWH nissî 'YHWH is my banner' — altar-name; one of the YHWH-compound altar-names of the Pentateuch (cf. YHWH-Yir'eh at Gen 22:14; YHWH-Shalom at Judg 6:24; YHWH-Tzidqenu at Jer 23:6).

16
And he said, "For a hand is upon the throne of YAH: YHWH will have war with Amaleq from generation to generation."
There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault it in thine own people.
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יָד֙ עַל־כֵּ֣ס יָ֔הּ מִלְחָמָ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה בַּֽעֲמָלֵ֑ק מִדֹּ֖ר דֹּֽר׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 16

The textually-difficult closing: MT preserves kî-yāḏ ʿal-kēs yāh 'for a hand is upon the throne of YAH' (with the yāh shortened-tetragrammaton, the only YH occurrence in Exodus); the LXX/Samaritan/Syriac variant reads nēs 'banner' (harmonizing with the YHWH-Nissi altar-name at v 15). See the overlay entry kes-yah-vs-nes-yah-textual-variant-exodus-17-16-overlay. The MT lectio difficilior is preserved per Childs 1974, Propp 1999, Sarna 1991.

Chapter 19

Exodus 19 — The Sinai theophany (the descent of YHWH on the mountain in fire, smoke, and trumpet-blast)

1
In the third month after the children of Yisra'el had gone out from the land of Mitsrayim, on that same day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh: for by a strong hand shall he let them go, and by a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לְצֵ֥את בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
Notes Verse 1

Arrival at the wilderness of Sinai 'on that same day' (ba-yyôm ha-zzeh) — the exact Sivan-1 reading is a documented rabbinic tradition (b. Shabbat 86b) supporting the Pentecost-as-Sinai theological identification.

2
And they journeyed from Refidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai, and they camped in the wilderness; and Yisra'el camped there before the mountain.
And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am Jehovah:
וַיִּסְע֣וּ מֵרְפִידִ֗ים וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ מִדְבַּ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיִּֽחַן־שָׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נֶ֥גֶד הָהָֽר׃
3
And Moses went up to the Elohim, and YHWH called to him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Ya'aqov, and tell the children of Yisra'el:
and I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Jehovah I was not known to them.
וּמֹשֶׁ֥ה עָלָ֖ה אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ מִן־הָהָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לְבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְתַגֵּ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Notes Verse 3

Moses' first ascent to hā-ʾĕlōhîm; YHWH calls min-hā-hār 'from the mountain' — establishing the mountain-as-divine-residence/theophany-site register.

4
'You yourselves have seen what I did to Mitsrayim, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
And I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, wherein they sojourned.
אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לְמִצְרָ֑יִם וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ עַל־כַּנְפֵ֣י נְשָׁרִ֔ים וָאָבִ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
Notes Verse 4

ʿal-kanp̄ê nĕšārîm 'on eagles' wings' — the nešer lexeme covers both 'eagle' and 'griffon-vulture' in Hebrew biological-classification (Sarna 1991 ad loc.; the modern critical literature documents the nešer as more probably 'griffon-vulture' on the basis of the bird's behavior at Job 39:27-30, Mic 1:16). The WoH-Translation preserves 'eagles' wings' per the dominant English-translation tradition.

5
And now, if you will surely listen to my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my treasured possession out of all the peoples — for all the earth is mine —
And moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.
וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּקֹלִ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֑י וִהְיִ֨יתֶם לִ֤י סְגֻלָּה֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים כִּי־לִ֖י כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Notes Verse 5

The covenantal-formula initiation: wi-hyiyṯem lî sĕgullâ mi-kkol hā-ʿammîm 'you shall be my treasured-possession from among all the peoples'. The sĕgullâ lexeme has Akkadian cognate-evidence: sikiltu 'private-treasure / personal-valuable'. See the central entry segullah-mamleḵet-kohanim-vegoy-qadosh-covenantal-formula-ex-19-5-6-cross-corpus. The conditional ʾim 'if' grammar is preserved.

6
and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words that you shall speak to the children of Yisra'el."
Wherefore say unto the children of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
וְאַתֶּ֧ם תִּהְיוּ־לִ֛י מַמְלֶ֥כֶת כֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְג֣וֹי קָד֑וֹשׁ אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Notes Verse 6

mamleḵeṯ kōhănîm wĕ-gôy qāḏôš 'a kingdom of priests and a holy nation'. Cross-corpus to Deut 7:6, 14:2, 26:18; Ps 135:4; 1 Pet 2:9 (the NT reapplication); Rev 1:6, 5:10. The central entry documents the disavowal against Christian-supersessionist 'Israel-replaced-by-Church' pre-resolution and against 'Israel = engineered-elect-race' Raëlian-canon reading.

7
And Moses came and called for the elders of the people and set before them all these words which YHWH had commanded him.
and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah your God, who bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֖א לְזִקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֣שֶׂם לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
8
And all the people answered together and said, "All that YHWH has spoken we will do." And Moses brought back the words of the people to YHWH.
And I will bring you in unto the land which I sware to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for a heritage: I am Jehovah.
וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
9
And YHWH said to Moses, "Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also trust in you forever." And Moses told the words of the people to YHWH.
And Moses spake so unto the children of Israel: but they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י בָּ֣א אֵלֶיךָ֮ בְּעַ֣ב הֶֽעָנָן֒ בַּעֲב֞וּר יִשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ בְּדַבְּרִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־בְּךָ֖ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיַּגֵּ֥ד מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
Notes Verse 9

ʾānōḵî bāʾ ʾēleḵā bĕ-ʿaḇ he-ʿānān 'I am coming to you in a thick cloud' — the cloud-theophany announcement-formula. See the central entry sinai-theophany-ex-19-elohim-craft-descent-disavowals-volcanic-hypothesis-cross-corpus.

10
And YHWH said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments.

And let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day YHWH will come down before the eyes of all the people on Mount Sinai.

Notes Verse 11

YHWH's third-day descent on Mount Sinai lĕ-ʿênê ḵol-hā-ʿām 'before the eyes of all the people' — the public-theophany framing.

12
And you shall set bounds for the people round about, saying, 'Take heed for yourselves not to go up into the mountain or to touch its edge; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
And Moses spake before Jehovah, saying, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips?
וְהִגְבַּלְתָּ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ סָבִ֣יב לֵאמֹ֔ר הִשָּׁמְר֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם עֲל֥וֹת בָּהָ֖ר וּנְגֹ֣עַ בְּקָצֵ֑הוּ כָּל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּהָ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
13
No hand shall touch him, for he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether animal or man, he shall not live.' When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they may go up to the mountain."
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
לֹא־תִגַּ֨ע בּ֜וֹ יָ֗ד כִּֽי־סָק֤וֹל יִסָּקֵל֙ אוֹ־יָרֹ֣ה יִיָּרֶ֔ה אִם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה אִם־אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יִחְיֶ֑ה בִּמְשֹׁךְ֙ הַיֹּבֵ֔ל הֵ֖מָּה יַעֲל֥וּ בָהָֽר׃
Notes Verse 13

bi-mšōḵ ha-yōḇēl 'when the ram's horn sounds a long blast' — the yōḇēl lexeme distinguished from the more-general šōp̄ār (vv 16, 19); see the overlay entry. The yōḇēl-Jubilee thematic-connection (Lev 25:9-13).

And Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and consecrated the people; and they washed their garments.
These are the heads of their fathers` houses. The sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
וַיֵּ֧רֶד מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִן־הָהָ֖ר אֶל־הָעָ֑ם וַיְקַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְכַבְּס֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָֽם׃

And he said to the people, "Be ready for the third day; do not approach a woman."

וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֱי֥וּ נְכֹנִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים אַֽל־תִּגְּשׁ֖וּ אֶל־אִשָּֽׁה׃
16
And it came to pass on the third day, when the morning came, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of a shofar exceedingly loud; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were a hundred thirty and seven years.
וַיְהִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י בִּֽהְיֹ֣ת הַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְהִי֩ קֹלֹ֨ת וּבְרָקִ֜ים וְעָנָ֤ן כָּבֵד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר וְקֹ֥ל שֹׁפָ֖ר חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
Notes Verse 16

THE SINAI THEOPHANY climax-verse. qōlōṯ ū-ḇĕrāqîm wĕ-ʿānān kāḇēḏ ʿal-hā-hār wĕ-qōl šōp̄ār ḥāzāq mĕʾōḏ 'thunders and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of a shofar exceedingly loud'. The Exodus-distinctive cloud-fire-thunder-trumpet-blast compositional cluster (overlay entry); the broader divine-self-revelation theophany (central entry). The qōlōṯ 'thunders' renders the Hebrew qôl in the standard theophanic register (cf. Ps 29); the synaesthesia rōʾîm ʾeṯ-ha-qōlōṯ 'seeing the thunders' (Ex 20:18) reactivates the same lexeme. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement of the Raëlian-canon's engagement — Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet engages this verse as the canon's most-explicit 'Elohim-craft descent on the mountain' citation — per the Shi'ur Qomah parasangs precedent and the Qur'an inshiqāq al-qamar precedent. The WoH-Translation does NOT adopt the canon's framing on the surface; the lens-discipline rides entirely in the apparatus.

17
And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet the Elohim, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
וַיּוֹצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֧ה אֶת־הָעָ֛ם לִקְרַ֥את הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּתַחְתִּ֥ית הָהָֽר׃
Notes Verse 17

Moses brings the people to meet hā-ʾĕlōhîm at the foot of the mountain (tachtit hā-hār) — the cultic-architectural staging of the theophany.

18
And Mount Sinai was wholly in smoke, because YHWH had come down upon it in fire; and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled exceedingly.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were a hundred thirty and three years.
וְהַ֤ר סִינַי֙ עָשַׁ֣ן כֻּלּ֔וֹ מִ֠פְּנֵי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרַ֥ד עָלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַיַּ֤עַל עֲשָׁנוֹ֙ כְּעֶ֣שֶׁן הַכִּבְשָׁ֔ן וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד כָּל־הָהָ֖ר מְאֹֽד׃
Notes Verse 18

wĕ-har sînay ʿāšan kullô mip-pĕnê ʾăšer yāraḏ ʿālāyw YHWH bā-ʾēš 'and Mount Sinai was wholly in smoke, because YHWH had come down upon it in fire'. The mountain-on-fire imagery; the simile kĕ-ʿešen ha-kkiḇšān 'like the smoke of a furnace' has cross-corpus echo at Gen 19:28 (the Sodom-Gomorrah destruction). The volcanic-Sinai academic-historical hypothesis (Stade, Wellhausen, Gressmann, Phythian-Adams, Humphreys 2003) is preserved as a documented academic-historical hypothesis without adjudication; see the central entry.

Notes Verse 19

The continued shofar-blast intensification; hā-ʾĕlōhîm yaʿănennû bĕ-qōl 'the Elohim answered him by a voice' — the Sinai-theophany dialogue-mediation.

Notes Verse 20

wa-yyēreḏ YHWH ʿal-har sînay 'YHWH came down on Mount Sinai' — the explicit descent-formula. The Moses-up / YHWH-down-summit meeting establishes the prophetic-mediator institutional grounding.

And YHWH said to Moses, "Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to YHWH to look, and many of them fall.
And the sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה רֵ֖ד הָעֵ֣ד בָּעָ֑ם פֶּן־יֶהֶרְס֤וּ אֶל־יְהוָה֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְנָפַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ רָֽב׃

And Moses said to YHWH, "The people are not able to come up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, 'Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
And Aaron took him Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל הָעָ֔ם לַעֲלֹ֖ת אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינָ֑י כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה הַעֵדֹ֤תָה בָּ֙נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַגְבֵּ֥ל אֶת־הָהָ֖ר וְקִדַּשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

And YHWH said to him, "Go, get down, and you shall come up — you and Aharon with you; but let not the priests and the people break through to come up to YHWH, lest he break out against them."
And the sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.

And Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

Chapter 20

Exodus 20 — The Decalogue + the altar law

1
And the Elohim spoke all these words, saying:
And Jehovah said unto Moses, See, I have made thee as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹֽר׃ (ס)
Notes Verse 1

The Decalogue-speech introduction. The Hebrew text uses ʾĕlōhîm (not YHWH) as the speech-introduction subject — a Priestly-source feature. The threefold enumeration-traditions (Jewish-Masoretic; Augustinian/Catholic/Lutheran; Orthodox/Reformed) are documented at the central entry aseret-ha-dvarim-decalogue-enumeration-jewish-vs-augustinian-orthodox-cross-corpus. The WoH-Translation preserves the Jewish-Masoretic enumeration per the source-text.

2
"I am YHWH your Elohim, who brought you out from the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves.
Thou shalt speak all that I command thee; and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
אָֽנֹכִ֖י֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֣֥ית עֲבָדִֽ֑ים׃
Notes Verse 2

The First Word (Jewish enumeration) / Prologue (Augustinian-Reformed enumeration). ʾānōḵî YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā ʾăšer hôṣēʾṯîḵā mē-ʾereṣ miṣrayim mibbêṯ ʿăḇāḏîm 'I am YHWH your Elohim, who brought you out from the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves'. See the central entries for the multi-tradition enumeration documentation (no adjudication) and the ʾānōḵî YHWH divine self-identification formula's cross-corpus reach to the Holiness Code, Deutero-Isaiah, Ezek 20.

3
You shall have no other elohim before my face.
And I will harden Pharaoh`s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה־לְךָ֛֩ אֱלֹהִ֥֨ים אֲחֵרִ֖֜ים עַל־פָּנָֽ֗יַ
Notes Verse 3

The no-other-elohim prohibition. lōʾ yihĕyeh lĕḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy 'you shall have no other elohim before my face'. The literal ʾĕlōhîm plural-translation and the literal ʿal-pānāy 'before my face' are preserved; the monolatry-vs-monotheism scholarly dispute (Smith 2002, Albertz 1994) is documented at the central entry without adjudication.

4
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, nor any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or what is in the earth beneath, or what is in the waters beneath the earth.
But Pharaoh will not hearken unto you, and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth my hosts, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
לֹֽ֣א תַֽעֲשֶׂ֨ה־לְךָ֥֣ פֶ֣֙סֶל֙ ׀ וְכָל־תְּמוּנָ֡֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤֣ר בַּשָּׁמַ֣֙יִם֙ ׀ מִמַּ֡֔עַל וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר֩ בָּאָ֖֨רֶץ מִתַָּ֑֜חַת וַאֲשֶׁ֥֣ר בַּמַּ֖֣יִם ׀ מִתַּ֥֣חַת לָאָֽ֗רֶץ
Notes Verse 4

The image-prohibition. The doubled pesel + tĕmûnâ construct is preserved. See the central entry pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus for the Mettinger 1995 No Graven Image? framework, the cross-corpus reach to Deut 4:15-19 and the Golden-Calf incident (Ex 32), and the prophetic anti-idolatry polemic tradition.

5
You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them; for I, YHWH your Elohim, am a jealous El, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, upon the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me,
And the Egyptians shall know that I am Jehovah, when I stretch forth my hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחְוֶ֥֣ה לָהֶ֖ם֮ וְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑ם֒ כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל־בָּנִ֛ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽ֑י׃
Notes Verse 5

ʾēl qannāʾ 'a jealous El' — the El-as-divine-name preservation. The poqed ʿawon 'visiting iniquity' formula across three-and-four generations; cross-corpus to Ex 34:7, Num 14:18, Deut 5:9; the prophetic-reversal at Ezek 18, Jer 31:29-30.

6
and showing chesed to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
And Moses and Aaron did so; as Jehovah commanded them, so did they.
וְעֹ֥֤שֶׂה חֶ֖֙סֶד֙ לַאֲלָפִ֑֔ים לְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי׃ (ס)
7
You shall not lift up the name of YHWH your Elohim in vain, for YHWH will not hold guiltless the one who lifts up his name in vain.
And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.
לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לַשָּׁ֑וְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 7

The name-of-YHWH-in-vain prohibition. lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ ʾeṯ-šēm-YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā la-ššāwʾ 'you shall not lift up the name of YHWH your Elohim in vain'. The literal lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ 'you shall not lift up' is preserved rather than the colloquial 'you shall not take'. See the central entry for the perjury-reading vs profane-utterance reading dispute and the post-biblical Tetragrammaton-substitution tradition.

8
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
זָכ֛וֹר֩ אֶת־י֥֨וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖֜ת לְקַדְּשֽׁ֗וֹ
Notes Verse 8

The Sabbath commandment with creation-grounding (Ex 20:8-11). The Deut 5:12-15 parallel grounds the Sabbath in the Exodus-deliverance instead. The rabbinic zakhor-shamor reconciliation 'remember and observe were said in a single utterance' (b. Rosh Hashanah 27a) harmonizes the two versions. See the central entry for the dual-grounding theological-significance.

9
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Show a wonder for you; then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.
שֵׁ֤֣שֶׁת יָמִ֣ים֙ תַּֽעֲבֹ֔ד֮ וְעָשִׂ֖֣יתָ כָּל־מְלַאכְתֶּֽךָ֒
10
but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your Elohim; you shall not do any work — you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your animal, nor the sojourner who is within your gates.
And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so, as Jehovah had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
וְי֙וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔֜י שַׁבָּ֖֣ת ׀ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑֗יךָ לֹֽ֣א־תַעֲשֶׂ֣֨ה כָל־מְלָאכָ֡֜ה אַתָּ֣ה ׀ וּבִנְךָֽ֣־וּ֠בִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤֨ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֜֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔֗ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖֙ אֲשֶׁ֥֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽ֔יךָ
11
For in six days YHWH made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore YHWH blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers: and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did in like manner with their enchantments.
כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת־יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖נַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י עַל־כֵּ֗ן בֵּרַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וַֽיְקַדְּשֵֽׁהוּ׃ (ס)
Notes Verse 11

The Sabbath-rest grounded in the six-days-of-creation pattern (Gen 2:1-3). The cosmological-anthropological universal significance contrasts with the Deut 5:15 social-historical liberation-significance.

12
Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land which YHWH your Elohim gives you.
For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron`s rod swallowed up their rods.
כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ (ס)
Notes Verse 12

Honor-parents (Fifth Word in Jewish, Augustinian, and Orthodox/Reformed enumerations alike). The kabbed (Piʿel) 'honor / treat-as-weighty' verb; the long-life land-promise lĕ-maʿan yaʾăriḵûn yāmêḵā establishes the consequence-of-obedience pattern that recurs throughout the Deuteronomic tradition.

13
You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
And Pharaoh`s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
לֹ֥֖א תִּֿרְצָֽ֖ח׃ (ס) לֹ֣֖א תִּֿנְאָֽ֑ף׃ (ס) לֹ֣֖א תִּֿגְנֹֽ֔ב׃ (ס) לֹֽא־תַעֲנֶ֥ה בְרֵעֲךָ֖ עֵ֥ד שָֽׁקֶר׃ (ס)
Notes Verse 13

The murder/adultery/theft/false-witness prohibitions. In MT verse-numbering all four are one verse (20:13); the English-translation tradition splits them (20:13/14/15/16). The WoH-Translation preserves MT-numbering per the source-text Masoretic convention. The rṣḥ 'to murder' decision (overlay entry ratsach-murder-vs-kill-decalogue-translation-convention-exodus-overlay) preserves the modern critical rṣḥ-as-unlawful-killing-specifically reading.

14
You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor."
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Pharaoh`s heart is stubborn, he refuseth to let the people go.
לֹ֥א תַחְמֹ֖ד בֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־תַחְמֹ֞ד אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֶ֗ךָ וְעַבְדּ֤וֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ֙ וְשׁוֹר֣וֹ וַחֲמֹר֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְרֵעֶֽךָ׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 14

The Tenth Word (Jewish enumeration) / Ninth-and-Tenth (Augustinian enumeration) / Tenth (Orthodox-Reformed enumeration). The chamad 'to covet' verb with the contested psychological-state vs action-oriented semantic range; see the overlay entry.

15
And all the people were seeing the thunders and the torches, and the sound of the shofar, and the mountain smoking; and the people saw and trembled, and they stood at a distance.
Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning; lo, he goeth out unto the water; and thou shalt stand by the river`s brink to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent shalt thou take in thy hand.
וְכָל־הָעָם֩ רֹאִ֨ים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹ֜ת וְאֶת־הַלַּפִּידִ֗ם וְאֵת֙ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וְאֶת־הָהָ֖ר עָשֵׁ֑ן וַיַּ֤רְא הָעָם֙ וַיָּנֻ֔עוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ מֵֽרָחֹֽק׃
Notes Verse 15

The synaesthesia: wĕ-ḵol-hā-ʿām rōʾîm ʾeṯ-ha-qōlōṯ 'and all the people were seeing the thunders'. The 'seeing the thunders' synaesthesia is a deliberate rhetorical-theological move (the people experience the theophany as a multi-sensory event in which the visual and auditory registers cross). The lapidim 'torches/lightnings' deploys the storm-theophany imagery.

16
And they said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will listen; but let the Elohim not speak with us, lest we die."
And thou shalt say unto him, Jehovah, the God of the Hebrews, hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou hast not hearkened.
וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה דַּבֵּר־אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְנִשְׁמָ֑עָה וְאַל־יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּ֛נוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים פֶּן־נָמֽוּת׃
17
And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear, for it is in order to test you that the Elohim has come, and in order that the fear of him may be on your faces, that you may not sin."
Thus saith Jehovah, In this thou shalt know that I am Jehovah: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in my hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־הָעָם֮ אַל־תִּירָאוּ֒ כִּ֗י לְבַֽעֲבוּר֙ נַסּ֣וֹת אֶתְכֶ֔ם בָּ֖א הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבַעֲב֗וּר תִּהְיֶ֧ה יִרְאָת֛וֹ עַל־פְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י תֶחֱטָֽאוּ׃
18
And the people stood at a distance, but Moses drew near to the thick darkness where the Elohim was.
And the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.
וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הָעָ֖ם מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ נִגַּ֣שׁ אֶל־הָֽעֲרָפֶ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 18

The ʿărāp̄el 'thick darkness / dense cloud' divine-presence indicator: Moses approaches the ʿărāp̄el where the Elohim is. Cross-corpus to 1 Kgs 8:12 (Solomon's temple-dedication theophany), Ps 18:9 ('thick darkness was under his feet'), Ps 97:2 ('clouds and thick darkness are round about him'), Joel 2:2, Zeph 1:15. The Moses-as-mediator institutional grounding for the prophetic office is established.

19
And YHWH said to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra'el: 'You yourselves have seen that I have spoken with you from the heavens.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם כִּ֚י מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עִמָּכֶֽם׃
Notes Verse 19

min-ha-šāmayim dibbartî ʿimmāḵem 'I have spoken with you from the heavens'. The from-the-heavens designation locates the divine speech in the cosmological-heavens register; cross-corpus to Deut 4:36.

20
You shall not make alongside me elohim of silver, and elohim of gold you shall not make for yourselves.
And Moses and Aaron did so, as Jehovah commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּן אִתִּ֑י אֱלֹ֤הֵי כֶ֙סֶף֙ וֵאלֹהֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃
Notes Verse 20

ʾĕlōhê ḵesep̄ wē-ʾlōhê zāhāḇ 'elohim of silver and elohim of gold' — preserves the elohim-plural for foreign-gods. Cross-corpus to the Golden-Calf incident (Ex 32) and the broader anti-idolatry polemic.

21
An altar of earth you shall make for me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
And the fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians could not drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
מִזְבַּ֣ח אֲדָמָה֮ תַּעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֒ וְזָבַחְתָּ֣ עָלָ֗יו אֶת־עֹלֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמֶ֔יךָ אֶת־צֹֽאנְךָ֖ וְאֶת־בְּקָרֶ֑ךָ בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַזְכִּ֣יר אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י אָב֥וֹא אֵלֶ֖יךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּֽיךָ׃
Notes Verse 21

The altar law: mizbaḥ ʾăḏāmâ 'an altar of earth' — the simple-earth-altar regulation. Cross-corpus to Deut 27:5-6, Josh 8:30-31 (Joshua's Mt-Ebal altar) — the cross-corpus deployment of the altar-law in the Joshua-land-entry narrative.

22
And if you make for me an altar of stones, you shall not build them of hewn stone; for if you have wielded your sword upon it, you have profaned it.
And the magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments: and Pharaoh`s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as Jehovah had spoken.
וְאִם־מִזְבַּ֤ח אֲבָנִים֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֔י לֹֽא־תִבְנֶ֥ה אֶתְהֶ֖ן גָּזִ֑ית כִּ֧י חַרְבְּךָ֛ הֵנַ֥פְתָּ עָלֶ֖יהָ וַתְּחַֽלְלֶֽהָ׃
Notes Verse 22

The no-hewn-stone altar law: lōʾ-ṯiḇneh ʾeṯhen gāzîṯ 'you shall not build them of hewn stone'. The profanation-by-iron-tool rationale; cross-corpus to 1 Macc 4:47 (Maccabean rebuilding of the altar per these terms).

23
And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed upon it."
And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he lay even this to heart.
וְלֹֽא־תַעֲלֶ֥ה בְמַעֲלֹ֖ת עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֑י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־תִגָּלֶ֥ה עֶרְוָתְךָ֖ עָלָֽיו׃ (פ)
Notes Verse 23

The no-steps-on-altar law: the nakedness-exposure rationale. The Hebrew Bible's cultic-modesty regulation; cross-corpus to Ex 28:42-43 (the priestly-undergarments regulation for the same nakedness-on-altar concern).

Contents

    Wheel of Heaven is an open, multilingual reading of the ancient world's creation traditions — Raëlian, biblical, Mesopotamian, and others — through a single working hypothesis: that the beings called Elohim were a small advanced human civilization that came here, designed life on Earth, and left a record in the religious texts. The reading runs across twelve ages of the precessional cycle, from the project's beginning twenty-two thousand years ago to the present age of disclosure and into the long future the next Great Year is opening. The site is free, source-aware, and built so the work can be checked.
